notes.loanToDepositRatio: Computed as gross loans (residential mortgages $277,246M + personal $46,388M + credit card $20,226M + business & government $210,047M = $553,907M, before allowance for credit losses) ÷ total deposits ($743,446M), per CIBC's unaudited consolidated balance sheet as at July 31, 2024.
notes.retailDepositsPct: Personal deposits ($250,231M) ÷ total deposits ($743,446M) per balance sheet Deposits note.
notes.wholesaleDepositsPct: Business and government ($414,178M) + Bank ($27,503M) + Secured borrowings ($51,534M) = $492,215M, ÷ total deposits $743,446M. 'Secured borrowings' (covered bond/securitization deposit notes) is treated as wholesale since it is not personal/retail.
notes.newMetricsSource: CIBC Report to Shareholders for the Third Quarter, 2024 (unaudited interim consolidated financial statements) — https://www.cibc.com/content/dam/cibc-public-assets/about-cibc/investor-relations/pdfs/quarterly-results/2024/q324report-en.pdf
notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: CIBC "Structural interest rate sensitivity – measures" table (Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders, disclosed quarterly). CIBC discloses only a +/-100bp parallel shock (2 of the 6 Basel scenarios). Most adverse: +100bp parallel increase gives EVE impact of -$1,325M (pre-tax, total CAD+USD) ÷ Tier 1 capital $48,751M (same report's capital table / Pillar 3 KM1) = -2.72%. Not equivalent to the worst of six Basel scenarios — CIBC shows only 2 of the 6 standard shocks. This %-of-Tier-1 framing is ours.
notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same +/-100bp parallel-shock table. Worse of the two disclosed scenarios: -100bp parallel decrease gives projected 12-month NII impact of -$271M (pre-tax, total CAD+USD) ÷ Tier 1 capital $48,751M = -0.56%. A derived ratio for cross-bank comparability; CIBC does not itself express NII sensitivity as a percentage of any base.
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: CIBC's disclosed "wholesale funding sources" contractual-maturity table total of $200,394M at carrying value (Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders) ÷ total assets $1,021,407M = 19.62%. Excludes repo (CIBC's own table scope), matching CIBC's existing method. CIBC discloses this table every quarter.
notes.stableDepositsPct: Stable deposits: unweighted $99,127M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q3 2024, CIBC Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $432,912M) = 22.9%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.
notes.lessStableDepositsPct: Less stable deposits: unweighted $117,113M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q3 2024, CIBC Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $432,912M) = 27.05%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.
notes.operationalDepositsPct: Operational deposits (all counterparties): unweighted $110,273M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q3 2024, CIBC Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $432,912M) = 25.47%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.
notes.nonOperationalDepositsPct: Non-operational deposits (all counterparties): unweighted $106,399M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q3 2024, CIBC Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $432,912M) = 24.58%. notes.source: All ratios/figures pulled from the nine-quarter 'Financial Highlights' and 'Balance sheet quality and liquidity measures' trend tables in CIBC's Q2 2026 Supplementary Financial Information package, cross-checked against the Q4/FY2024 news release.
notes.loanToDepositRatio: Gross loans (res. mortgages $280,672M + personal $46,681M + credit card $20,551M + business & government $214,299M = $562,203M) ÷ total deposits ($764,857M), per CIBC 2024 Annual Report consolidated balance sheet, Oct 31 2024.
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: CIBC's own disclosed 'wholesale funding sources' contractual-maturity table (deposits from banks, CDs/commercial paper, bearer deposit notes/BAs, senior unsecured MTNs/structured notes, covered bonds, mortgage/cards securitization, subordinated liabilities) totaled $215,317M at carrying value as at Oct 31, 2024 ÷ total assets $1,041,985M. This CIBC-defined figure excludes repo ($110,153M); including repo per the broader task definition gives (215,317+110,153)/1,041,985 = 31.23%. Reporting the narrower, CIBC-labeled figure as primary.
notes.retailDepositsPct: Personal deposits ($252,894M) ÷ total deposits ($764,857M), balance sheet basis.
notes.wholesaleDepositsPct: Business & government ($435,499M) + Bank ($20,009M) + Secured borrowings ($56,455M) ÷ total deposits $764,857M, balance sheet basis. An alternative LCR-scope calc (see stable/less-stable/operational/non-operational below) gives retail 49.70%/wholesale 50.30% on a 3-month-average, LCR-defined-category basis — materially different because the LCR categorization uses average balances and different bucketing rules.
notes.stableDepositsPct: OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months ended Oct 31 2024: Stable deposits $98,592M (unweighted) as % of total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $437,287M).
notes.lessStableDepositsPct: Less stable deposits $118,722M (unweighted) / $437,287M LCR-scope deposit total.
notes.operationalDepositsPct: Operational deposits (all counterparties, incl. cooperative bank networks) $115,421M (unweighted) / $437,287M.
notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: CIBC does not disclose the full 6-scenario Basel/OSFI IRRBB1 template (parallel up/down, steepener, flattener, short rate up/down) — it only discloses a +/-100bp parallel shock under 'Structural Interest Rate Risk (SIRR)'. Most adverse of the two disclosed scenarios: +100bp parallel increase gives EVE impact of -$1,356M (pre-tax, total CAD+USD), vs -100bp giving +$1,237M. -$1,356M / Tier 1 capital $49,481M (Q4/25 Pillar 3 KM1 table, Q4/24 column) = -2.74%. Not equivalent to 'worst of six Basel scenarios' — CIBC only shows 2 of the 6 standard shocks.
notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same +/-100bp parallel shock table. Worse of the two scenarios: -100bp parallel decrease gives projected 12-month NII impact of -$242M (pre-tax, total). As % of Tier 1 capital ($49,481M) for comparability = -0.49%; CIBC itself does not express NII sensitivity as a % of any capital or income base — this is a derived ratio.
notes.newMetricsSource: CIBC 2024 Annual Report (audited consolidated financial statements and MD&A) and CIBC Q4/25 Pillar 3 Report — https://www.cibc.com/content/dam/cibc-public-assets/about-cibc/investor-relations/pdfs/quarterly-results/2024/ar-24-en.pdf

Worse of the two disclosed scenarios: -100bp parallel decrease gives projected 12-month NII impact of -$164M (pre-tax, total CAD+USD) ÷ Tier 1 capital $56,067M = -0.29%. A derived ratio for cross-bank comparability; CIBC does not itself express NII sensitivity as a percentage of any base.
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: CIBC's disclosed "wholesale funding sources" contractual-maturity table total of $227,468M at carrying value (Q2 2026 Report to Shareholders) ÷ total assets $1,160,560M = 19.6%. Excludes repo (CIBC's own table scope), matching CIBC's existing method. CIBC discloses this table every quarter.
notes.stableDepositsPct: Stable deposits: unweighted $102,406M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q2 2026, CIBC Q2 2026 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $492,675M) = 20.79%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.
notes.lessStableDepositsPct: Less stable deposits: unweighted $138,131M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q2 2026, CIBC Q2 2026 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $492,675M) = 28.04%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.
notes.operationalDepositsPct: Operational deposits (all counterparties): unweighted $145,304M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q2 2026, CIBC Q2 2026 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $492,675M) = 29.49%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.
notes.nonOperationalDepositsPct: Non-operational deposits (all counterparties): unweighted $106,834M (OSFI LCR common disclosure template, average of the three months in Q2 2026, CIBC Q2 2026 Report to Shareholders — disclosed quarterly) ÷ total LCR-scope deposits (stable+less stable+operational+non-operational = $492,675M) = 21.68%. Denominator = sum of the four LCR categories, matching CIBC's existing method.

irrbbDisclosureNote: CIBC discloses interest rate risk in the banking book under the heading 'Structural interest rate sensitivity' in the MD&A of its Report to Shareholders every quarter (and again in the Annual Report at the Oct 31 fiscal year-end). It shows a single prescribed shock size (immediate and sustained +/-100 basis points, floored at zero), reporting both the projected 12-month pre-tax ΔNII and the pre-tax ΔEVE for each direction, split by CAD and USD. It does not publish the full Basel Committee six-scenario IRRBB1 standardized table (parallel up/down, steepener, flattener, short-rate up/down). This is industry-wide in Canada, not CIBC-specific: OSFI's Pillar 3 Disclosure Guideline for D-SIBs is only now (2026 consultation, comment period closed July 20, 2026) proposing to adopt the BCBS IRRBB1 template, with an expected effective date of fiscal Q4 2027 — so no current Canadian D-SIB publicly discloses the full six-scenario table yet. CIBC's disclosed sensitivities are not expressed as a percentage of any capital base by CIBC itself; the %-of-Tier-1 figures here are derived by dividing CIBC's disclosed dollar sensitivities by Tier 1 capital from the same report's capital table, for cross-bank comparability.
